analysis.title: Silver: The reset isn't over
key_insights: Silver is testing a major trend line and trades well below its 200-day moving average. A close below $60 would be a negative technical development, with $56 the next support.
The dollar is a short-term headwind for silver. Silver and the inverted DXY track each other closely, though current dollar levels do not by themselves imply silver must fall immediately.
GS notes that stronger dollar environments have historically coincided with managed-money long liquidation in silver.
Speculative positioning deteriorated sharply. Managed Money, Other and Non-Reportable traders sold a combined $1.6bn in the final week of September, the largest weekly selling since February.
The $1.6bn was split evenly between long liquidation ($800mn) and new shorts ($800mn), so new bears entered the trade rather than only longs taking profit.
GS estimates CTAs have been cutting silver exposure as the technical picture weakens. Further weakness could trigger another wave of systematic selling.
Silver implied volatility has returned to where it started before the mania that began about a year ago, after surging from around 37 to a peak of 110.
Downside protection remains expensive. GS notes normalized 25-delta put-call skew has richened into its top decile over the past two years, even though headline vol has collapsed.
risk_factors: A close below $60 in silver, with $56 the next support.
A stronger dollar, which has historically coincided with managed-money long liquidation.

New short positioning is building, not only long liquidation.
vol_and_positioning: Silver implied vol surged from around 37 to a peak of 110 and is now back near the starting level of about 37.
Normalized 25-delta put-call skew in silver is in its top decile over the past two years, so downside protection is expensive despite low headline vol.

tension_points.bull_case: Headline implied vol has fully normalized to pre-mania levels and the speculative excess has been partly cleared by $1.6bn of selling.
tension_points.bear_case: New shorts entered, CTAs are cutting exposure, the dollar is a headwind and skew shows elevated demand for downside protection, so another leg lower may be needed to clear the decks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A close below $60 would confirm further downside toward $56.
